items.title: HAL headers declare the interfaces the units use
items.objective: Show by inspection that include/hal_cpu.h, hal_gpio.h, hal_wdg.h, hal_timer.h, hal_usart.h, hal_rcc.h, hal_store.h, hal_store_ex.h, hal_mem.h, hal_task.h and hal_diag_wake.h only declare functions and constants, define no function and hold no data, and that no header contains a register name or fixed address.
preconditions: include/ is at the revision under test
steps: Open each hal_*.h header listed in SWU-HAL-001 and check that it contains only declarations, macros and typedefs.
Search the headers for register names, offsets or fixed addresses.
expected: every listed header declares only functions, macros and types
no header defines a function or a variable
no register name, offset or fixed address appears in any header

items.title: hal_store_ex.h declares only the per-part read
items.objective: Show by inspection that include/hal_store_ex.h declares hal_store_read_parts and the validity bit macros (HS_VALID_HEADER, HS_VALID_ENTRY_SHIFT, HS_VALID_ALL = 0x01FF) and defines no function and no data.
preconditions: include/hal_store_ex.h is at the revision under test
steps: Check the declaration of hal_store_read_parts and the three macros; check that no function body or variable definition exists.
expected: hal_store_read_parts is declared as uint16_t hal_store_read_parts(hi_retained_t *out)
HS_VALID_ALL equals 0x01FF (header bit plus eight history slot bits)
the header defines no function and holds no data

items.title: crc32_init returns the initial value
items.objective: Show that crc32_init returns 0xFFFFFFFF.

items.title: CRC-32/MPEG-2 check value of the ASCII digits 1-9
items.objective: Show that folding the nine bytes '1'..'9' into the initial context gives the CRC-32/MPEG-2 check value 0x0376E6E7 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, no reflection, no final XOR).

items.title: Chunked update equals the one-shot value
items.objective: Show that the context carried across two consecutive chunks gives the same value as one call over the whole range.

items.title: crc32_update with NULL data returns the context
items.objective: Show that a NULL data pointer returns ctx unchanged.

items.title: crc32_update with length 0 returns the context
items.objective: Show that len 0 returns ctx unchanged (lower boundary minus one).

items.title: crc32_update above the maximum length returns the context
items.objective: Show that len 1048577 (one above the maximum) returns ctx unchanged.

items.title: crc32_update accepts the maximum length
items.objective: Show that len 1048576 is processed (upper boundary) by comparing the one-shot value with two chunks of 524288 bytes over a zero-filled buffer.
steps: ctx = two chained calls of 524288 bytes.

items.title: A single byte changes the context
items.objective: Show that len 1 (lower boundary) is processed and the context changes.

items.title: Default table passes cfg_init
items.objective: Show that cfg_default_table with CFG_DEFAULT_COUNT entries is accepted: HI_OK, valid, count 4, no fault notified.
preconditions: configuration INVALID, fault manager in STARTUP
expected: fm_get_state() == HI_STATE_STARTUP and no retained write

items.title: Default table content
items.objective: Show that cfg_default_table holds T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT (10 ms, start limit 200 units, execution limit 300 units) and T_DIAG (100 ms, 200, 2000 units) in release order.
steps: Read the four entries of cfg_default_table.
expected: names T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, T_DIAG in that order
start limits 200 units each; execution limits 300, 300, 300, 2000 units

items.title: Accessors on a valid table
items.objective: Show that cfg_get returns the entry pointers and cfg_period_ticks returns period_ms / 10 for valid tasks.

items.title: Accessors with a task index at and above the count
items.objective: Show that task 4 (count) and 255 give NULL and 0.

items.title: Accessors on an INVALID configuration
items.objective: Show that every accessor returns 0 or NULL before a successful cfg_init.

items.title: cfg_init rejects a NULL table
items.objective: Show that table NULL gives HI_E_RANGE, stays INVALID and notifies fault code 9 once.
expected: fm_get_state() == HI_STATE_SAFE and one retained write (one notification)

items.title: cfg_init rejects count 0
items.objective: Show that count 0 (one below the minimum) gives HI_E_RANGE and a code 9 notification.

items.title: cfg_init rejects count 5
items.objective: Show that count 5 (one above the maximum) gives HI_E_RANGE and a code 9 notification.

items.title: cfg_init accepts count 1
items.objective: Show that a single valid entry (lower count boundary) is accepted.
expected: cfg_get(0) is the entry, cfg_get(1) == NULL

items.title: Unknown task name is rejected
items.objective: Show that the name T_X (not one of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, T_DIAG) gives HI_E_RANGE and a code 9 notification.
steps: Call cfg_init with one entry named T_X.

items.title: Empty task name is rejected
items.objective: Show that an empty name is an unknown task and is rejected.
steps: Call cfg_init with one entry with an empty name.

items.title: Unterminated task name is rejected without reading beyond index 6
items.objective: Show that a 7-character name without NUL that starts like T_CTRL is rejected.
steps: Call cfg_init with one entry named 'T_CTRLX' (seven characters, no NUL).

items.title: Name that is a prefix of a known name is rejected
items.objective: Show that T_CT (NUL where T_CTRL continues) differs from every known name.
steps: Call cfg_init with one entry named T_CT.

items.title: Period 0 is rejected
items.objective: Show that period_ms 0 gives HI_E_RANGE and a code 9 notification.

items.title: Period that is not a multiple of 10 ms is rejected
items.objective: Show that period_ms 15 gives HI_E_RANGE.

items.title: Period above 65535 ticks is rejected
items.objective: Show that period_ms 655360 (65536 ticks, one above the counter range) gives HI_E_RANGE.

items.title: Period of 65535 ticks with limits equal to the period is accepted
items.objective: Show that period_ms 655350 and both limits 65535000 units (equal to the period) are accepted.
steps: Call cfg_init with T_IN, 655350 ms, limits 65535000.

items.title: Start limit above the period is rejected
items.objective: Show that start_limit_u 1001 with period 10 ms (1000 units) is rejected.
steps: Call cfg_init with T_IN, 10 ms, start limit 1001, execution limit 300.

items.title: Execution limit above the period is rejected
items.objective: Show that exec_limit_u 1001 with period 10 ms and a valid start limit is rejected.
steps: Call cfg_init with T_IN, 10 ms, start limit 200, execution limit 1001.

items.title: Limits equal to the period are accepted
items.objective: Show that start and execution limits of 1000 units with period 10 ms (not longer than the period) are accepted.
steps: Call cfg_init with T_IN, 10 ms, limits 1000 and 1000.

items.title: One invalid entry among valid ones rejects the table
items.objective: Show that a table of two entries whose second has period 7 ms is rejected as a whole.
steps: Call cfg_init(table of T_IN valid and T_CTRL period 7, 2).

items.title: A failed cfg_init clears the previous table
items.objective: Show that after a valid table a failing cfg_init leaves the configuration INVALID.
steps: Call cfg_init with an entry of period 0.

items.title: oc_init configures all three pins low
items.objective: Show that oc_init calls hal_gpio_config_output_low for pins 0, 1, 2 and returns HI_OK.
expected: three configure calls in the order pin 0, 1, 2

items.title: oc_init reports a failing pin and still attempts all pins
items.objective: Show that a refused configuration of pin 1 gives HI_E_HW after all three pins were attempted.

items.title: oc_init reports a failing first pin
items.objective: Show that a refused configuration of pin 0 does not stop the other pins and gives HI_E_HW.

items.title: oc_init clears the safe-state flag
items.objective: Show that after oc_safe_state the status request is refused and after oc_init it is accepted again.

items.title: oc_safe_state drives all pins low in one critical section
items.objective: Show that oc_safe_state writes low to the three pins between one enter and one exit of the critical section.
expected: three hal_gpio_write calls, all pin levels low
event order: critical enter, three writes, critical exit, nothing else

items.title: oc_safe_state ignores write failures and is idempotent
items.objective: Show that failing pin writes do not stop the command, a repeated call writes again, and the flag is still set.
steps: Make writes succeed and call oc_status_high().

items.title: oc_status_high drives only the status pin high
items.objective: Show that with flag clear and state STARTUP the status pin goes high, the control pins stay low and the write is inside the critical section.
preconditions: flag clear, fault manager in STARTUP
expected: exactly one write; status pin high, CTRL1 and CTRL2 low
the write lies between the outermost critical enter and exit; depth 0 afterwards

items.title: oc_status_high reports a failing status pin write
items.objective: Show that a refused status pin write returns HI_E_HW and leaves the critical section.

items.title: oc_status_high is refused when the safe-state flag is set
items.objective: Show that with the flag set (state STARTUP) the request returns HI_E_REFUSED and changes no pin.
preconditions: oc_safe_state called, fault manager in STARTUP
expected: no hal_gpio_write call, status pin low

items.title: oc_status_high is refused in state SAFE
items.objective: Show that with the flag clear and fault state SAFE the request returns HI_E_REFUSED and changes no pin.
preconditions: one detection notified, oc_init called (flag clear)

items.title: oc_status_high is refused in state LATCHED
items.objective: Show that with the flag clear and fault state LATCHED the request returns HI_E_REFUSED and changes no pin.

items.title: ws_init clears the inhibit flag
items.objective: Show that ws_init returns HI_OK and clears the flag set by ws_inhibit.

items.title: ws_init clears the window-enabled state
items.objective: Show that after ws_init the next cycle service enables the window watchdog again instead of refreshing.
preconditions: window watchdog enabled by a first cycle service
expected: one enable call, no refresh call

items.title: ws_activate configures the window and starts the independent watchdog
items.objective: Show that ws_activate calls hal_wwdg_configure(6, 12) then hal_iwdg_start(100) and returns HI_OK.
expected: window configured with lower 6 ms, upper 12 ms
hal_iwdg_start called once with 100 ms, after the window configuration

items.title: ws_activate with a refused window configuration
items.objective: Show that a refused window configuration returns HI_E_HW and the independent watchdog is not started.

items.title: ws_activate with a refused independent watchdog start
items.objective: Show that a refused hal_iwdg_start returns HI_E_HW.
expected: window configuration called once, start called once

items.title: ws_startup_service services the independent watchdog in one critical section
items.objective: Show that with the flag clear ws_startup_service issues one independent-watchdog service inside one critical section and nothing else.
expected: event order: critical enter, hal_iwdg_service, critical exit
no window enable or refresh call

items.title: ws_startup_service issues nothing while inhibited
items.objective: Show that with the flag set no service command is issued.

items.title: First ws_cycle_service enables the window watchdog
items.objective: Show that the first call enables the window watchdog and services the independent watchdog in the same critical section.
expected: one enable call, no refresh call, one independent service
event order: critical enter, window enable, independent service, critical exit

items.title: Later ws_cycle_service calls refresh the window watchdog
items.objective: Show that the second call refreshes the window watchdog and services the independent watchdog, without a second enable.
expected: enable count stays 1, refresh count 1, independent services 2
event order: critical enter, window refresh, independent service, critical exit

items.title: Refused window enable returns HI_E_HW and is retried
items.objective: Show that a refused enable returns HI_E_HW with the independent watchdog still serviced, and the enable is retried at the next call.
steps: Make enable succeed, call ws_cycle_service() again.
expected: first call returns HI_E_HW, one independent service, no refresh
second call returns HI_OK with a second enable call and no refresh

items.title: ws_cycle_service issues nothing while inhibited
items.objective: Show that with the flag set the call returns HI_OK and issues no enable, refresh or service command.
expected: no enable, refresh or independent service call

items.title: Inhibit after the window is enabled stops refresh and service
items.objective: Show that once inhibited, neither cycle nor start-up service issues a command, also when the window watchdog was already enabled.
expected: no independent service and no window refresh

items.title: Inhibit flag is idempotent and persistent
items.objective: Show that ws_is_inhibited is false after init, true after ws_inhibit (also repeated) and stays true after a cycle service.
steps: Read the flag; call ws_inhibit() twice; read the flag; call ws_cycle_service(); read the flag.

items.title: ts_init starts the timer and clears the compare
items.objective: Show that ts_init starts the time base through the HAL, clears the compare event and returns HI_OK.

items.title: ts_init returns the HAL error unchanged
items.objective: Show that ts_init returns HI_E_HW when hal_timer_start fails and does not clear the compare.

items.title: ts_init disarms events and restarts the count from counter 0
items.objective: Show that a second ts_init disarms every slot and zeroes the ms count, remainder and last reading so the origin is counter value 0.
preconditions: ts_init done, time 250 units, one event armed
steps: Call ts_ms (2), arm tag 5, call ts_init again, call ts_pop_due at 1000, call ts_ms at the same time.
expected: ts_pop_due returns false and tag unchanged
ts_ms after re-init == 2 (time counted from counter 0)

items.title: ts_now_u returns the HAL reading
items.objective: Show that ts_now_u returns hal_timer_read unchanged, including the maximum value.
steps: Set time 12345, call ts_now_u; set time 0xFFFFFFFF, call ts_now_u.

items.title: ts_ms accumulates milliseconds with a carried remainder
items.objective: Show that ts_ms divides units by 100 and carries the remainder so the value never exceeds real elapsed time.

items.title: ts_ms is correct across the 32-bit counter wrap
items.objective: Show that ts_ms uses the modular difference of readings across the counter wrap.
steps: Set time 0xFFFFFF00, call ts_ms; set time 100, call ts_ms.
expected: second value 42949673 (356 units elapsed plus remainder 40 gives 3 ms)

items.title: ts_ms runs in one critical section
items.objective: Show that ts_ms enters and leaves exactly one critical section and restores the previous state.

items.title: ts_elapsed_u with a NULL mark returns 0
items.objective: Show that ts_elapsed_u(NULL) returns 0.

items.title: ts_elapsed_u returns 0 for a zero difference
items.objective: Show that a zero difference returns 0 and the mark stays at now.

items.title: ts_elapsed_u returns the difference minus one unit and moves the mark
items.objective: Show that the result is diff - 1 for diff > 0 (1 gives 0) and the mark is stored.
steps: Call ts_elapsed_u(&mark); set time 151; call again.

items.title: ts_elapsed_u uses the modular difference across the wrap
items.objective: Show that a mark before the wrap and a reading after it give diff - 1.

items.title: ts_arm refuses a tag above 32

steps: Call ts_arm(33, 10) and ts_arm(255, 10); call ts_pop_due.

items.title: ts_arm accepts the highest tag 32
items.objective: Show that tag 32 (cycle end) arms and the compare is programmed to its instant.

items.title: ts_arm enforces the scheduling horizon
items.objective: Show that an instant 0x40000000 units ahead is refused (nothing armed) and 0x3FFFFFFF ahead is accepted.

items.title: ts_arm treats a past instant as due at once
items.objective: Show that an instant before now is accepted, programmed, and returned by ts_pop_due.

items.title: Compare is programmed to the earliest armed event
items.objective: Show that with two armed events the compare holds the earlier instant (the later one armed second).
steps: Arm tag 1 at 1010 and tag 2 at 1020.

items.title: Compare selection uses wrapped distances
items.objective: Show that an event armed second with the smaller wrapped distance replaces the compare, across the counter wrap.

items.title: Re-arming a tag replaces its instant
items.objective: Show that a second ts_arm of the same tag changes the instant of the slot.
steps: Arm tag 7 at 200, then at 300; pop at 250 and at 300.

items.title: ts_cancel of an armed event clears the compare
items.objective: Show that cancelling the only armed event returns true and clears the compare.

items.title: ts_cancel reprograms the compare to the remaining event
items.objective: Show that cancelling one of two events moves the compare to the other.
preconditions: tag 4 at 200 and tag 5 at 300 armed

items.title: ts_cancel of an event never armed returns false
items.objective: Show that cancelling an unarmed tag returns false and changes no compare.
expected: compare set and clear not called

items.title: ts_cancel with a tag above 32 returns false
items.objective: Show that tags 33 and 255 return false without entering a critical section.

items.title: ts_cancel of a decided or already cancelled event returns false
items.objective: Show that an event removed by ts_pop_due, or cancelled before, is no longer pending.
preconditions: tag 4 armed in the past, tag 5 armed ahead

items.title: ts_pop_due with a NULL tag returns false
items.objective: Show that a NULL tag pointer returns false and removes nothing.
steps: Call ts_pop_due(100, NULL), then with a valid pointer.

items.title: ts_pop_due with nothing due leaves the tag unchanged
items.objective: Show that an armed event ahead of now is not returned and *tag is unchanged.

items.title: ts_pop_due removes the due event and clears the compare
items.objective: Show that the due event is returned once, disarmed and the compare cleared.

items.title: ts_pop_due returns the earliest instant first (higher tag earlier)
items.objective: Show that tag 5 at 80 is returned before tag 3 at 90.
preconditions: tag 3 at 90 and tag 5 at 80 armed

items.title: ts_pop_due returns the earliest instant first (lower tag earlier)
items.objective: Show that tag 3 at 80 is returned before tag 5 at 90.
preconditions: tag 3 at 80 and tag 5 at 90 armed

items.title: Equal instants give the lower tag first
items.objective: Show that start (2), execution (17) and cycle-end (32) events with one instant are returned in tag order.

items.title: A not-yet-due event stays armed and the compare moves to it
items.objective: Show that after the due event is popped the compare holds the remaining future event.
preconditions: tag 1 at 50 and tag 9 at 200 armed, time 10

items.title: tsup_init clears the release state

items.title: tsup_init switches alive supervision off

items.title: tsup_enable_alive runs in one critical section
items.objective: Show that tsup_enable_alive enters and leaves one critical section.

items.title: tsup_on_release rejects an unconfigured task

items.title: tsup_on_release arms the start-limit event one unit after the limit

items.title: First release with alive on raises nothing

items.title: Fault 1 is raised once

items.title: Missed counter saturates at 255

items.title: tsup_on_start without a release returns HI_E_STATE

items.objective: Show that an execution event with no stored start raises nothing.

decisions.text: The HAL is replaced by tests/fakes/fake_hal.h, one header included once per test program. It defines every function declared in include/hal_*.h, records calls, arguments and an ordered event log, and returns values set through the global fk (default: every call succeeds, time 0, store invalid, USART accepts everything and is idle). The other units are linked in unchanged (all src/**/*.c are compiled into every program) and are observed through the HAL fakes.
decisions.rationale: Units reach hardware only through the HAL headers (DEC-SWU-001). Fidelity limits (UVR-03): no real peripheral timing, no interrupt preemption (the critical section fake only counts nesting), no real memory-mapped registers, no reset (hal_rcc_request_reset returns), time advances only by the fixed step the test sets.

decisions.text: Cases are independent: each case calls the init functions of the unit under test and of the collaborators it uses and calls fk_reset(); no case depends on the state left by another.
decisions.rationale: UVR order independence; the hi_test.h harness prints one HI-TEST line per case.

decisions.text: In cfg_name_equal the loop-exit outcome of the condition i <= HI_NAME_MAX (index 7 reached) has no test: the loop is left earlier by a differing character or by the NUL of the known name, because every known name (T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, T_DIAG) has its NUL at index 6 or lower, so any name that matches up to index 6 breaks at the NUL.
decisions.rationale: Defensive loop bound required by the design (no read beyond index 6); the exit is unreachable with the constant known-name table. Statement coverage is complete; the unreachable branch is recorded here instead of excluding the file.
